name: Chapter 4: Animal Kingdom
description: Basis of classification, every non-chordate phylum, chordates and the vertebrate classes

cards.term: About how many animal species have been described?
cards.definition: Over a million

cards.term: Name the fundamental features used as the basis of animal classification.
cards.definition: Arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, and patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems

cards.text: Levels of organisation: sponges show {{c1::cellular}} level, coelenterates {{c2::tissue}} level, Platyhelminthes {{c3::organ}} level, and annelids to chordates {{c4::organ system}} level.

cards.term: What is the cellular level of organisation?
cards.definition: Cells arranged as loose cell aggregates, with some division of labour, e.g. sponges

cards.term: What is the tissue level of organisation?
cards.definition: Cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, e.g. coelenterates

cards.term: Why is the digestive system of Platyhelminthes called incomplete?
cards.definition: It has a single opening that serves as both mouth and anus

cards.term: What is a complete digestive system?
cards.definition: One with two openings: mouth and anus

cards.term: What is an open circulatory system?
cards.definition: Blood is pumped out of the heart and cells and tissues are directly bathed in it

cards.term: What is a closed circulatory system?
cards.definition: Blood circulates through a series of vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries)

cards.term: What is an asymmetrical animal? Example?
cards.definition: No plane through the centre divides it into equal halves, e.g. most sponges

cards.term: What is radial symmetry? Which groups show it?
cards.definition: Any plane through the central axis gives two identical halves: coelenterates, ctenophores, echinoderms

cards.term: What is bilateral symmetry? Examples?
cards.definition: Identical left and right halves in only one plane: annelids, arthropods

cards.term: Echinoderms: radial or bilateral?
cards.definition: Adults radial, larvae bilateral

cards.term: What are diploblastic animals? Example?
cards.definition: Cells in two embryonic layers, external ectoderm and internal endoderm, e.g. coelenterates

cards.term: What lies between ectoderm and endoderm in diploblastic animals?
cards.definition: An undifferentiated layer, the mesoglea

cards.term: What are triploblastic animals? Which phyla?
cards.definition: The embryo has a third layer, mesoderm, between ectoderm and endoderm: Platyhelminthes to chordates

cards.term: Figure 4.2 · Germinal layers: (a) diploblastic, (b) triploblastic
What is a coelom?
cards.definition: A body cavity between body wall and gut wall, lined by mesoderm

cards.term: Name the coelomate phyla.
cards.definition: Annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates, chordates

cards.term: What is a pseudocoelom? Example?
cards.definition: A body cavity not lined by mesoderm; mesoderm lies as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm. e.g. Aschelminthes

cards.term: Which animals are acoelomates?
cards.definition: Those with no body cavity, e.g. Platyhelminthes

cards.term: Figure 4.3 · Sectional view: name each body plan
What is metameric segmentation? Example?
cards.definition: Body divided externally and internally into segments with serial repetition of some organs, e.g. earthworm. The phenomenon is metamerism.

cards.term: In which phylum is segmentation first seen?
cards.definition: Annelida

cards.term: What is the notochord?
cards.definition: A mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development

cards.term: Which phyla are non-chordates?
cards.definition: Porifera to Echinodermata (and Hemichordata)

cards.term: Figure 4.4: broad classification of Kingdom Animalia. Trace the path to Annelida.
cards.definition: Organ system level → bilateral → true coelom (coelomate) → Annelida

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a), (b), (c).
cards.definition: Porifera: (a) Sycon (b) Euspongia (c) Spongilla

cards.term: What is the common name of Porifera? Habitat and symmetry?
cards.definition: Sponges; generally marine, mostly asymmetrical

cards.text: In sponges, water enters through minute pores, {{c1::ostia}}, into a central cavity, the {{c2::spongocoel}}, and goes out through the {{c3::osculum}}.

cards.term: What does the canal system of sponges help with?
cards.definition: Food gathering, respiratory exchange, removal of waste

cards.term: Which cells line the spongocoel and canals?
cards.definition: Choanocytes (collar cells)

cards.term: Is digestion in sponges intracellular or extracellular?
cards.definition: Intracellular

cards.term: What is the skeleton of sponges made of?
cards.definition: Spicules or spongin fibres

cards.term: Are sponges unisexual or hermaphrodite? Fertilisation and development?
cards.definition: Hermaphrodite fertilisation internal development indirect (larval stage)

cards.term: Give the common names: Sycon, Spongilla, Euspongia.
cards.definition: Sycon (Scypha), Spongilla (fresh water sponge), Euspongia (bath sponge)

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a) and (b) and their body forms.
cards.definition: Coelenterata: (a) Aurelia (medusa) (b) Adamsia (polyp)

cards.term: From what is the name 'Cnidaria' derived?
cards.definition: The cnidoblasts (cnidocytes), which contain stinging capsules (nematocysts)

cards.term: What are cnidoblasts used for?
cards.definition: Anchorage, defence, capture of prey

cards.term: Level of organisation and germ layers of cnidarians?
cards.definition: Tissue level; diploblastic

cards.term: Where is the mouth of a cnidarian?
cards.definition: On the hypostome, opening into a central gastro-vascular cavity

cards.term: Is digestion in cnidarians intracellular or extracellular?
cards.definition: Both

cards.term: What is the skeleton of corals made of?
cards.definition: Calcium carbonate

cards.term: Compare the polyp and medusa forms.
cards.definition: Polyp: sessile, cylindrical (Hydra, Adamsia). Medusa: umbrella-shaped, free-swimming (Aurelia).

cards.term: What is metagenesis? Example?
cards.definition: Alternation of generations: polyps produce medusae asexually, medusae form polyps sexually, e.g. Obelia

cards.text: Cnidarians: {{c1::Physalia}} is the Portuguese man-of-war, {{c2::Adamsia}} the sea anemone, {{c3::Pennatula}} the sea-pen, {{c4::Gorgonia}} the sea-fan and {{c5::Meandrina}} the brain coral.

cards.term: Which phylum is this animal from? Name it.
cards.definition: Ctenophora: Pleurobrachia

cards.term: Common names of ctenophores?
cards.definition: Sea walnuts or comb jellies

cards.term: What helps ctenophores move?
cards.definition: Eight external rows of ciliated comb plates

cards.term: Which property is well marked in ctenophores?
cards.definition: Bioluminescence: emitting light

cards.term: Ctenophores: sexes, reproduction, fertilisation?
cards.definition: Sexes not separate only sexual reproduction fertilisation external, indirect development

cards.term: Name two ctenophores.
cards.definition: Pleurobrachia, Ctenoplana

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Platyhelminthes: (a) tapeworm (Taenia) (b) liver fluke (Fasciola)

cards.term: Why are Platyhelminthes called flatworms?
cards.definition: Their body is dorso-ventrally flattened

cards.term: Symmetry, germ layers, coelom and level of Platyhelminthes?
cards.definition: Bilateral, triploblastic, acoelomate, organ level

cards.term: Which features of parasitic flatworms suit parasitism?
cards.definition: Hooks and suckers; some absorb nutrients directly through the body surface

cards.term: Which cells help flatworms in osmoregulation and excretion?
cards.definition: Flame cells

cards.term: Which flatworm has high regeneration capacity?
cards.definition: Planaria

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Which is male and female?
cards.definition: Aschelminthes (roundworm). Females are often longer than males.

cards.term: Why are aschelminthes called roundworms?
cards.definition: Body is circular in cross-section

cards.term: Coelom of roundworms?
cards.definition: Pseudocoelomate

cards.term: Describe the alimentary canal of roundworms.
cards.definition: Complete, with a well-developed muscular pharynx

cards.term: How are body wastes removed in roundworms?
cards.definition: An excretory tube removes them through the excretory pore

cards.term: Are roundworms monoecious or dioecious?
cards.definition: Dioecious: sexes separate

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Annelida: (a) Nereis (b) Hirudinaria

cards.term: What does 'Annelida' mean?
cards.definition: Latin annulus: little ring (body marked into segments, metameres)

cards.term: Annelids: coelom and segmentation?
cards.definition: Coelomate, metamerically segmented

cards.term: What are parapodia? In which annelid?
cards.definition: Lateral appendages for swimming, in aquatic Nereis

cards.term: Circulatory system of annelids?
cards.definition: Closed

cards.term: Which organs help annelids in osmoregulation and excretion?
cards.definition: Nephridia

cards.term: Describe the neural system of annelids.
cards.definition: Paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord

cards.term: Which annelid is dioecious, and which are monoecious?
cards.definition: Nereis is dioecious; earthworms and leeches are monoecious

cards.text: Annelida: {{c1::Pheretima}} is the earthworm and {{c2::Hirudinaria}} the blood sucking leech.

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a)–(d).
cards.definition: Arthropoda: (a) locust (b) butterfly (c) scorpion (d) prawn

cards.term: Which is the largest phylum of Animalia?
cards.definition: Arthropoda: over two-thirds of all named species

cards.term: What covers the body of arthropods?
cards.definition: A chitinous exoskeleton

cards.term: What does 'Arthropoda' mean?
cards.definition: Jointed appendages (arthros: joint, poda: appendages)

cards.term: Name the respiratory organs of arthropods.
cards.definition: Gills, book gills, book lungs, tracheal system

cards.term: Circulatory system of arthropods?
cards.definition: Open

cards.term: What are the excretory organs of arthropods?
cards.definition: Malpighian tubules

cards.term: What are statocysts?
cards.definition: Balancing organs (sensory organs of arthropods)

cards.term: Name three mosquito vectors.
cards.definition: Anopheles, Culex, Aedes

cards.term: Which arthropod is a gregarious pest?
cards.definition: Locusta (locust)

cards.term: Which arthropod is a living fossil?
cards.definition: Limulus (king crab)

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Mollusca: (a) Pila (b) Octopus

cards.term: Which is the second largest animal phylum?
cards.definition: Mollusca

cards.term: Body plan of a mollusc?
cards.definition: Covered by a calcareous shell; unsegmented, with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump

cards.term: What is the mantle, and the mantle cavity?
cards.definition: Mantle: soft spongy skin over the visceral hump. The space between hump and mantle is the mantle cavity, with feather-like gills.

cards.term: What do the gills of molluscs do?
cards.definition: Respiratory and excretory functions

cards.term: What is the radula?
cards.definition: A file-like rasping organ in the mouth, for feeding

cards.text: Molluscs: {{c1::Pinctada}} pearl oyster, {{c2::Sepia}} cuttlefish, {{c3::Loligo}} squid, {{c4::Octopus}} devil fish, {{c5::Aplysia}} sea-hare, {{c6::Dentalium}} tusk shell, {{c7::Chaetopleura}} chiton.

cards.term: What is Pila?
cards.definition: Apple snail

cards.term: Which phylum is this? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Echinodermata: (a) Asterias (b) Ophiura

cards.term: Why the name 'Echinodermata'?
cards.definition: Spiny bodied: an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles

cards.term: Habitat of echinoderms?
cards.definition: All marine

cards.term: Where are the mouth and anus of echinoderms?
cards.definition: Mouth on the lower (ventral) side, anus on the upper (dorsal) side

cards.term: What is the most distinctive feature of echinoderms?
cards.definition: The water vascular system: locomotion, capture and transport of food, respiration

cards.term: Which system is absent in echinoderms?
cards.definition: Excretory system

cards.text: Echinoderms: {{c1::Asterias}} star fish, {{c2::Echinus}} sea urchin, {{c3::Antedon}} sea lily, {{c4::Cucumaria}} sea cucumber, {{c5::Ophiura}} brittle star.

cards.term: Where is Hemichordata placed now?
cards.definition: A separate phylum under non-chordata (earlier a sub-phylum of Chordata)

cards.term: What is the stomochord?
cards.definition: A rudimentary structure in the collar region, similar to the notochord

cards.term: Figure 4.15 · Balanoglossus
Circulatory system and excretory organ of hemichordates?
cards.definition: Circulation open; excretory organ: proboscis gland

cards.term: Name two hemichordates.
cards.definition: Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus

cards.term: Table 4.2: coelom
cards.definition: Porifera to Platyhelminthes: Absent; Aschelminthes: Pseudocoelomate; Annelida onwards: Coelomate

cards.definition: Annelida: Present; Arthropoda: Present; Chordata: Present; All others: Absent

cards.term: Match: operculum, parapodia, comb plates, radula, choanocytes.
cards.definition: Operculum: Osteichthyes. Parapodia: Annelida. Comb plates: Ctenophora. Radula: Mollusca. Choanocytes: Porifera.

cards.term: Figure 4.16 · Chordate characteristics
Three fundamental characters of chordates?
cards.definition: A notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits

cards.term: Besides the three basic features, what else do chordates possess?
cards.definition: A post anal tail and a closed circulatory system

cards.term: Table 4.1: chordates vs non-chordates
cards.definition: Notochord: Present (absent in non-chordates); Central nervous system: Dorsal, hollow, single (ventral, solid, double); Pharynx: Perforated by gill slits (absent); Heart: Ventral (dorsal, if present); Post-anal tail: Present (absent)

cards.term: Name the three subphyla of Chordata.
cards.definition: Urochordata (Tunicata), Cephalochordata, Vertebrata

cards.term: What are protochordates?
cards.definition: Urochordata and Cephalochordata: exclusively marine

cards.term: Where is the notochord in Urochordata and in Cephalochordata?
cards.definition: Urochordata: only in the larval tail. Cephalochordata: head to tail, throughout life.

cards.term: Name three urochordates and one cephalochordate.
cards.definition: Urochordata: Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum. Cephalochordata: Branchiostoma (Amphioxus / lancelet).

cards.term: Which protochordate is this?
cards.definition: Ascidia (Urochordata)

cards.term: What replaces the notochord in adult vertebrates?
cards.definition: A cartilaginous or bony vertebral column

cards.term: Justify: all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
cards.definition: Vertebrates have a notochord only in the embryo, replaced by a vertebral column; protochordates keep the notochord and have no vertebral column

cards.term: Features of vertebrates besides the basic chordate ones?
cards.definition: Ventral muscular heart (2, 3 or 4 chambers), kidneys, paired appendages (fins or limbs)

cards.term: Classification of subphylum Vertebrata
Which vertebrate is this, and what is special about its mouth?
cards.definition: Petromyzon (lamprey): sucking, circular mouth without jaws

cards.term: How do living cyclostomes live?
cards.definition: As ectoparasites on some fishes

cards.term: How many gill slits do cyclostomes have?
cards.definition: 6–15 pairs

cards.term: Do cyclostomes have scales and paired fins?
cards.definition: No. Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.

cards.term: Describe the spawning of cyclostomes.
cards.definition: Marine, but migrate to fresh water to spawn they die within a few days larvae return to the ocean after metamorphosis

cards.term: Name two cyclostomes.
cards.definition: Petromyzon (lamprey), Myxine (hagfish)

cards.term: Which class are these fishes? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Chondrichthyes: (a) Scoliodon (b) Pristis

cards.term: Endoskeleton and mouth position of Chondrichthyes?
cards.definition: Cartilaginous endoskeleton; mouth ventral

cards.term: Gill slits of cartilaginous fishes?
cards.definition: Separate, without operculum (gill cover)

cards.term: What are placoid scales, and what are the teeth of sharks?
cards.definition: Minute scales in the tough skin. Teeth are modified placoid scales, backwardly directed.

cards.term: Why must cartilaginous fishes swim constantly?
cards.definition: No air bladder, so they would sink

cards.term: Heart of fishes?
cards.definition: Two-chambered: one auricle, one ventricle

cards.term: What does poikilothermous mean?
cards.definition: Cold-blooded: unable to regulate body temperature

cards.term: What do the pelvic fins of male Chondrichthyes bear?
cards.definition: Claspers

cards.text: Chondrichthyes: {{c1::Torpedo}} has electric organs and {{c2::Trygon}} (sting ray) a poison sting.
{{c1::Scoliodon}} is the dog fish, {{c2::Pristis}} the saw fish, and {{c3::Carcharodon}} the great white shark.

cards.term: Which class are these? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Osteichthyes: (a) Hippocampus (sea horse) (b) Catla

cards.term: How many gills do bony fishes have, and what covers them?
cards.definition: Four pairs, covered by an operculum on each side

cards.term: Scales of bony fishes?
cards.definition: Cycloid or ctenoid

cards.term: What does the air bladder of bony fishes do?
cards.definition: Regulates buoyancy

cards.term: Fertilisation and development in bony fishes?
cards.definition: Fertilisation usually external mostly oviparous development direct

cards.term: Bony fishes: examples
cards.definition: Marine: Exocoetus (flying fish), Hippocampus (sea horse); Freshwater: Labeo (rohu), Catla (katla), Clarias (magur); Aquarium: Betta (fighting fish), Pterophyllum (angel fish)

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Osteichthyes

Give the NCERT examples.

MarineExocoetus (flying fish), Hippocampus (sea horse)
FreshwaterLabeo (rohu), Catla (katla), Clarias (magur)
AquariumBetta (fighting fish), Pterophyllum (angel fish)

cards.term: Which class are these? Name (a) and (b).
cards.definition: Amphibia: (a) Salamandra (b) Rana

cards.term: What does 'Amphibia' mean?
cards.definition: Gr. amphi: dual, bios: life. They live in water and on land.

cards.term: Skin, eyes and ear of amphibians?
cards.definition: Moist skin without scales eyes with eyelids a tympanum represents the ear

cards.term: What is the cloaca?
cards.definition: A common chamber into which the alimentary canal, urinary and reproductive tracts open

cards.term: Respiration in amphibians?
cards.definition: By gills, lungs and through skin

cards.term: Heart of amphibians?
cards.definition: Three-chambered: two auricles, one ventricle

cards.term: Fertilisation and development of amphibians?
cards.definition: Fertilisation external; oviparous; development indirect

cards.text: Amphibia: {{c1::Bufo}} toad, {{c2::Rana}} frog, {{c3::Hyla}} tree frog, {{c4::Salamandra}} salamander, {{c5::Ichthyophis}} limbless amphibian.

cards.term: Which class are these? Name (a)–(d).
cards.definition: Reptilia: (a) Chameleon (b) Crocodilus (c) Chelone (d) Naja

cards.term: What does 'Reptilia' refer to?
cards.definition: Their creeping or crawling locomotion (Latin repere / reptum)

cards.term: Skin of reptiles?
cards.definition: Dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes

cards.term: Do reptiles have external ear openings?
cards.definition: No. A tympanum represents the ear.

cards.term: Heart of reptiles?
cards.definition: Usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles

cards.term: Which reptiles shed their scales as skin cast?
cards.definition: Snakes and lizards

cards.text: Reptiles: {{c1::Chelone}} turtle, {{c2::Testudo}} tortoise, {{c3::Calotes}} garden lizard, {{c4::Hemidactylus}} wall lizard, {{c5::Chameleon}} tree lizard.

cards.term: Which class are these? Name (a)–(d).
cards.definition: Aves: (a) Neophron (b) Struthio (c) Psittacula (d) Pavo

cards.term: Characteristic features of birds?
cards.definition: Feathers, a beak, forelimbs modified into wings

cards.term: Which gland is present in the skin of birds?
cards.definition: Only the oil gland at the base of the tail

cards.term: What are pneumatic bones?
cards.definition: Hollow long bones with air cavities (birds)

cards.term: What extra chambers does the digestive tract of birds have?
cards.definition: Crop and gizzard

cards.term: What supplements respiration in birds?
cards.definition: Air sacs connected to the lungs

cards.term: What does homoiothermous mean?
cards.definition: Warm-blooded: able to maintain a constant body temperature

cards.term: Which modifications help birds fly?
cards.definition: Feathers, wings, pneumatic bones, air sacs, four-chambered heart, warm blood

cards.text: Birds: {{c1::Corvus}} crow, {{c2::Columba}} pigeon, {{c3::Psittacula}} parrot, {{c4::Struthio}} ostrich, {{c5::Pavo}} peacock, {{c6::Aptenodytes}} penguin, {{c7::Neophron}} vulture.

cards.term: Which class are these? Name (a)–(d).
cards.definition: Mammalia: (a) Ornithorhynchus (b) Macropus (c) Pteropus (d) Balaenoptera

cards.term: What is the most unique mammalian characteristic?
cards.definition: Mammary glands (milk-producing)

cards.term: Which features of the skin and ear are unique to mammals?
cards.definition: Skin with hair; external ears (pinnae)

cards.term: Which mammal is oviparous?
cards.definition: Ornithorhynchus (platypus)

cards.text: Mammals: {{c1::Macropus}} kangaroo, {{c2::Pteropus}} flying fox, {{c3::Balaenoptera}} blue whale, {{c4::Delphinus}} common dolphin, {{c5::Macaca}} monkey.

cards.term: Heart chambers in vertebrates
cards.definition: Fishes: 2; Amphibians: 3; Reptiles: 3 (4 in crocodiles); Birds, mammals: 4
